title: Operational basics: health, shutdown, strict migrations, version
description: Bring the server up to what an unattended instance needs. Add /healthz (cheap: database ping only) and point the container health check at it instead of rendering the home page. Shut down gracefully on SIGTERM/SIGINT so in-flight requests finish and the database closes. Make a migration failure stop startup (main.go:44-45 only logs a warning today). Inject the version, commit and build date at build time; show the version in the admin footer, at /version, and in `jim-dot-tennis version`. Stop logging every static file request and the VAPID key. Validate configuration at startup with messages a non-developer can act on.

recommended_model.name: Sonnet 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: A list of small, well-understood server changes.

acceptance_criteria: /healthz returns 200 only when the database is reachable and migrations are current; the Dockerfile has a HEALTHCHECK using it
SIGTERM completes in-flight requests within a timeout and exits 0
A failed or dirty migration prevents startup with a message that names the migration and the recovery steps
Version is visible in the admin footer, at /version and from the command line
Startup logs are a short, readable summary; static requests are not logged
CLAUDE.md no longer says dirty state is handled by forcing the version
testing_requirements: Manual: docker stop exits promptly and cleanly

context.user_story: As a club operator, I want to know what version I am running and that the service is healthy.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
